name: New York

statute.name: New York Freedom of Information Law

response.rule_text: Agency must within five business days grant, deny in writing, or acknowledge and give an approximate date; if granting, access within 20 business days of acknowledgment unless it gives written reasons and a specific date (Pub. Off. Law § 89(4)(a)).

fees.labor_rule: FOIL provides no search fees; for electronic records, lowest-paid qualified employee's hourly salary after two hours of staff time (§ 87(1)(c)).
fees.copy_rule: $0.25 per photocopy up to 9x14; actual reproduction cost for other records (§ 87(1)(b)(iii)).
fees.estimate_required: Advance notice required only if electronic records need over 2 hours staff time or outside service.
fees.late_penalty: Attorney fees under § 89(4)(c); mandatory where agency had no reasonable basis for denial (2017 amendment).

residency.rule_text: Records available to the public, individually and collectively; no residency limit stated.

appeal.body: Agency records appeals officer, then Article 78 proceeding in NY Supreme Court
appeal.rule_text: Appeal denial to the agency within 30 days (unit not labeled; calendar inferred); appeals officer decides in 10 business days (§ 89(4)(b)); then Article 78 within 4 months (CPLR 217). Committee on Open Government gives advisory opinions only.

format_rule: Agencies must provide records on the medium requested if they can reasonably make the copy (§ 87(5)); no obligation to create new records (§ 89(3)).
